The impact of acquiring these lands for right of way is felt in the division of existing holdings and the relocation of people and businesses. Land acquisition for the proposed project was proceeding under an approved Relocation Plan. Relocation Program Plans submitted to the Federal Highway Administration in September 1969 and updated in August 1971, March 1972, presented a detailed analysis of available housing, proposed displacements and services available to those concerned. The relocation plan and project assurance were found acceptable and approved by the Federal Highway Administration on September 5, 1969 and reaffirmed on August 23, 1971. Approval by the Misconsin Department of Local Affairs and Development was April 14, 1972. Eighteen (18) of the 51 parcels had already been acquired by March of 1973 when the Highway Commission suspended all right of way acquisitions until such time as a Final Environmental Impact Statement would be circulated and accepted. The remaining 33 parcels include 9 families and 2 businesses. Locations of lands to be acquired and displacements are shown in Figure 17. The Relocation Program Plan is contained in Appendix A and contains detailed information on the economic and social characteristics of the people and businesses to be displaced.
